subject: english-language
title: Stretch: Power in Texts Adventure
welcome_lead: Stretch — analyse power encoded in headlines, manifestos and political speeches.
meta_desc: GCSE English Language stretch — synthetic personalisation, ideology, lexical choice as power.
final_note: You explored synthetic personalisation, ideology and how lexical choice carries power in real texts.

concepts.def: Mass texts addressing 'you' to fake intimacy
Assumption built INTO the way something is said
Softening language to reduce force or claim

walkthroughs.body_html:
Adverts saying 'You deserve the best' fake one-to-one intimacy with millions.

Fairclough called this synthetic personalisation.

High modality: 'We MUST act now' (forceful, certain).

Low modality: 'We might perhaps consider...' (cautious).

Modal verbs encode power.

'When are you going to start working harder?' presupposes you AREN'T working hard.

Powerful — and slippery.

mcqs.q: An advert saying 'Treat YOURSELF — you deserve it' uses:
'You MUST do this' has what kind of modality?

numericals.q: How many main modality strengths do we usually contrast (high and low)?

free_texts.q: What's the term for an assumption built INTO a phrase (e.g. 'when did you stop lying?')? One word.
